content:
I know nearly nothing about GitHub Actions, Workflows, or CI in general. doc/dev/index.md in the the Lean 4 repository says:

It is also possible to generate releases that others can use, simply by pushing a tag to your fork of the Lean 4 github repository (and waiting about an hour; check the Actions tab for completion). If you push my-tag to a fork in your github account my_name, you can then put my_name/lean4:my-tag in your lean-toolchain file in a project using lake. (You must use a tag name that does not start with a numeral, or contain _).

That seems to not work. Recently, this workflow run, triggered by a push, failed. Because I wanted a public toolchain from the commit, I dared to make a draft PR with the same commit at lean#13914. There, all tests passed, and the generation of the toolchain was successful.

This looks like a flaky issue with the test script, the log shows

diff: /dev/fd/63: Bad file descriptor

A retry should help.

A retry should help

I might have been wrong here: the issue should be sticky in GitHub macOS runners (the behavior depends on the bash version). Cherry-picking my commit in the PR above might be worth a shot.

Thank you! Indeed, when I did re-run the workflow, the "build / macOS aarch64" job failed again, with at least very similar error messages.

I merged master and then cherry-picked your commit. This lead to this workflow run. This time "build / Linux fsantize" fails. The jobs for the pull request again produced no errors. I already tried to re-run the job once, which failed, too. The error messages of both attempts look very similar, although not exactly identical.
The async tests can be a bit flaky occasionally. This may be solved by more attempts.
lean4#13943 may help with flaky async tests (but due to the nature of the problem, it'll take a while to see whether it actually works).

The DNS test is surfacing a shutdown race (lean4#13939), I believe

SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior /home/runner/work/lean4/lean4/src/runtime/object.cpp:1295:21
--- -   2026-06-03 17:15:42.971358775 +0000
+++ async_dns.lean.out.produced 2026-06-03 17:15:42.967242658 +0000
@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+/home/runner/work/lean4/lean4/src/runtime/object.cpp:1295:21: runtime error: member call on null pointer of type 'lean::task_manager'
+SUMMARY: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: undefined-behavior /home/runner/work/lean4/lean4/src/runtime/object.cpp:1295:21
TEST FAILED: Unexpected output

Joscha Mennicken said:

The async tests can be a bit flaky occasionally. This may be solved by more attempts.

I tried it two more times, but with the same result.

Joscha Mennicken said:

lean4#13943 may help with flaky async tests (but due to the nature of the problem, it'll take a while to see whether it actually works).

After rebasing on master, including lean4#13943, it succeeded on the first try.

The resulting workflow is here. It has no errors anymore, but cancelled/skipped jobs. It still does not provide a release (elan toolchain install whxvd/lean4:message-fill fails with "error: binary package was not provided for 'linux'"). The job "build / Linux aarch64" gets cancelled, because it "has exceeded the maximum execution time while awaiting a runner for 24h0m0s". Could that be the reason?
Yes, you would have to change the os field to an available runner name or disable the entry

Thank you! I changed the relevant line in ci.yml from just "os": "nscloud-ubuntu-22.04-arm64-4x16" to "os": large ? "nscloud-ubuntu-22.04-arm64-4x16" : "ubuntu-24.04-arm", similar to the os value in the other builds. Unfortunatly, there is no GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest-arm, so a specific Ubuntu version had to be specified.

I encountered two more issues:

  • For the "Release" step of the release job to work in the fork, I had to enable read and write workflow permissions at https://github.com/whxvd/lean4/settings/actions.
  • The "Update release.lean-lang.org" step of the release job was run unconditionally, and failed the job. But it probably only makes sense if: github.repository == 'leanprover/lean4', so I added that. (This in a sense is only cosmetic, because the previous step did successfully produce the release.)

After that a build job failed rather early with "No space left on device". A re-run solved that.

Since I now have custom commits in my fork that adapt the CI, I added another one that disables all lengthy tests and checks and non-release builds.

It is also possible to generate releases that others can use, simply by pushing a tag to your fork of the Lean 4 github repository (and waiting about an hour; check the Actions tab for completion).
--doc/dev/index.md

That does not accurately state the current affairs. Nowadays, it is not "simply by pushing a tag".

If a PR with relevant changes to ci.yml, or a PR with an updated doc/dev/index.md in that regard would be appreciated, please let me know. But probably hardly anyone uses this feature of generating releases in a fork. So I think for now it is enough to just have this topic lingering on Zulip which can be found by searching for "release fork", and see what the future tells.
Thanks. Since we do have at least some of those switches in place, an update PR would be appreciated
